qualifying_individual_rule.value: An electrical contractor licence requires an associated Master Electrician, who may be associated with only ONE electrical contractor at a time; without one the contractor's licence is put on hold. A contractor based outside Michigan must hire a master who lives in Michigan.
qualifying_individual_rule.source_title: Electrical Examination, Licensing/Registration & Application Information — Michigan LARA BCC
qualifying_individual_rule.evidence: A Master Electrician can only associate with one Electrical Contractor at a time.
qualifying_individual_rule.note: This is the field that turns an acquisition into a licensing emergency, and Michigan states both halves of it: the master cannot be shared across two companies, and the company stops when the master does. The renewal page adds the second trigger — 'If the qualifying license lapses, your contractor license will be placed on hold until they renew, and you notify our office' — so the hold is not lifted by the master renewing; the company must also notify the bureau.

entity_registration.note: No entity-registration requirement is published by the bureau for electrical contractors.

per_location_rule.note: No per-location or per-branch rule is published for electrical contractors.

change_notification_deadline.note: No deadline is published for naming a replacement Master Electrician. What IS published is the consequence: the contractor licence goes on hold until the qualifying licence is renewed AND the bureau is notified. An indefinite hold with no clock is worse for the customer than a deadline, and the absence is recorded rather than a figure borrowed from another state.

typical_timeline.value: Up to 3–5 weeks for the Licensing Section to process an application, reviewed in order of receipt.
typical_timeline.source_title: Bureau of Construction Codes — Licensing Section, Michigan LARA
typical_timeline.evidence: our processing time may be up to 3-5 weeks and applications are reviewed in order of receipt
typical_timeline.note: This is the bureau's own published figure for reviewing the application, not an end-to-end time to a licence in hand: it excludes scheduling and sitting the PSI examination, and for plumbing the separate hands-on practical, whose 2026 dates run monthly and are capped at 50–100 candidates and repeatedly 'at capacity'. Application fees are non-refundable and duplicate applications slow the queue.

coverage_notes: Michigan's local layer is modelled only where the bureau names it. The City of Detroit is named, on the electrical page. Every other Michigan municipality and county is not covered.
No bond position and no liability-insurance minimum could be established from any bureau page or application form read; both are left empty rather than guessed or borrowed from a neighbouring state.

PSI examination fees are set and collected by PSI, not by the bureau, and are not in this record. Since 14 June 2017 the bureau says in terms that examination fees should no longer be sent to the State of Michigan.

Michigan's Skilled Trades Regulation Act (2016 PA 407) and the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Act (1972 PA 230) are named on the bureau's pages but were NOT fetched: legislature.mi.gov did not respond to either attempt on 2026-09-04. Every statutory citation in this record is quoted as the bureau reproduces it, never from the statute itself.

Fire Alarm Specialty Technician, Fire Alarm Contractor, Sign Specialist and Sign Specialty Contractor are issued on the same forms and renewed on the same page as the electrical credentials, and are NOT modelled here. A customer whose roster includes fire-alarm technicians will get nothing for them.
The City of Detroit's own electrical licences and registrations are named by the bureau and are not covered: the record says the city issues them and stops there.

pass_a.method: fetched each source with kb-scripts/lib_kb.fetch (serial, 1.5 s spacing, two attempts, no retry on 403/404), read the normalised text in full, and recorded each value with a verbatim evidence fragment checked against the normalised page before writing

pass_b.method: two checks. (1) kb-scripts/verify_pass_b.py re-fetches every source_url over the network, independently of the pass-A cache, and asserts the evidence fragment is still literally present. (2) a separate semantic re-read of every source, re-deriving each value from the page rather than from the record, recorded per value in kb-data/_verification/<record>.md. A disagreement in either check demotes the value.
